purpose: Primary-owned evidence gate; generic runner labels alone are not migration evidence. This specification does not modify runner classification.
scope: Apply independently to each actual candidate invocation in both frozen builds and modes. Use only that invocation's preconditions and raw observations.
prerequisite: An independent primary reviewer must implement and review this gate and verify paired guest evidence. Native ptrace and deterministic tracee ground truth were accepted for the literal requirements only. GNU strace was not executed, GNU equivalence is not claimed, and these non-root guest observations do not establish signal-delivery parity.
inputs: Exact suite and helper hashes, candidate build identity and complete per-case runner result, including setup status, runner error or timeout and stray-process information.

Raw captured bytes and missing/error/truncated flags for each diagnostic: setup-controls.json, parser-controls.json, gcc.out, gcc.err, direct.out, direct.err, direct.status, native.out, native.err, native.status, candidate.start, candidate.out, candidate.err, candidate.status and assertions.json, conditional on the reached stage.

The full assertions.json trace observations, including raw-offset result assignments for every surviving complete history, complete_history_count, transient_branch_steps, peak_live_histories, search_bound, child_initial_stops, events, complete syscall records and separate physical-line findings.
integrity_and_capability_inconclusive: Reject missing, stale, corrupt, oversized, truncated, hash-mismatched, unreadable or structurally invalid harness/control artifacts or records; missing actual invocation start/completion/status; runner timeout or other runner error; stray process; and any failed, timed-out or incomplete setup. Do not infer pass or product fail from a generic runner label in these cases.

For reached setup stages, verify stage order compile-1, compile-2, direct, native; each stage completion, timeout, expected status, command, output offset, byte count and SHA-256 against its actual raw bytes. Require direct exit 42, native exit 0, parser-controls completed with no error and exactly the named positive and negative controls in the pinned helper. Inspect native stdout identities and raw syscall log; verify the matching parent fork and child, exactly one STOP child 19 0, and that stop precedes the first child syscall stop. Fork-event and stop may be observed in either order; both must be present and tied to the same child. Cross-check setup-controls native_initial_stop fields and offsets against the native log.

Verify candidate.start mode, exact status syntax and agreement with assertions, all reported sizes/hashes against raw candidate files, complete=true and empty infrastructure_errors. A candidate invocation that did not return or has a missing or invalid status is inconclusive. Candidate timeout is inconclusive regardless of runner label.

Reject as inconclusive any attribution search bound, including token, stop, wait-entry or history limits. Keep its raw trace and recorded partial histories. For a purported semantic trace success require all_bytes_consumed=true, search_bound=false, valid complete-history records, complete_history_count equal to the number of complete histories and exactly one complete history. Validate each recorded entry and return offset and the whole raw trace against that history. Multiple surviving complete histories are inconclusive, not product failure. Transient branches do not by themselves disqualify a unique final history.

If an assertion reports a product mismatch but its completeness, setup capability or input integrity cannot be established, classify the case inconclusive until the missing prerequisite is resolved. Preserve the existing raw v2 evidence separately and do not accept it under these revised definitions.
product_assessment_after_integrity: Once control capability, complete invocation and raw-artifact integrity are independently established, compare the actual stdout identities/reap record, candidate status and raw trace against the asserted per-requirement observations. A missing child record, wrong status/identity/reap, malformed or incomplete trace, wrong or misplaced signal event, unexpected PID, unknown event or tracer-error text is a product mismatch; do not reclassify it as infrastructure merely because the trace is malformed.

On follow traces, accept zero to two child SIGSTOP events only before the child's first observed syscall, after the parent's fork entry, and with an observed fork event identifying that same child; event and stop records may occur in either order. More than two such pre-syscall stops exceed this fixture's explicit bound and are inconclusive, not evidence of a signal-delivery defect. Other SIGSTOP positions or PIDs remain product trace mismatches.

A successful case requires zero product_failures and one independently verified complete history. Preserve physical-line findings as separate observations; semantic reconstruction of interleaving does not prove a one-syscall-per-physical-line requirement.
setup_failure_diagnostics: Use setup-controls.json and the stage records to identify reached operations. Require parser-controls.json only if parser began, compiler outputs to the extent compilation reached them, and direct/native files only when those invocations were reached and produced them. Missing later-stage files after setup failure are expected; the failure and partial artifacts remain setup/infrastructure evidence and cannot establish candidate behavior.
